category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Missing Monitoring Data
prompt: A monitoring agent sends a normal value every minute. If consecutive missing data continues for a sufficient period, you want the existing CloudWatch alarm to enter ALARM after the last normal value falls outside the evaluation range. Which missing-data treatment should you use?

choices.text: Treat missing data as good
choices.explanation: The alarm may judge the monitored resource as normal even when it cannot send metrics.

choices.text: Treat missing data as ignore
choices.explanation: If the last state is OK, missing data will not cause the alarm to change to ALARM.

choices.text: Leave the evaluation period unset
choices.explanation: This does not provide a mechanism that eliminates the evaluation period, nor does it define how missing data is judged.

choices.text: Treat missing data as breaching
choices.explanation: A stopped observation can be included in the evaluation as a threshold violation.

learning.reason: A stopped observation can be evaluated as a threshold violation.
learning.concept: The meaning of missing data depends on the metric. For metrics emitted only when an anomaly occurs, treating missing data as normal may be appropriate.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Connection Without a Bastion Host
prompt: An operator periodically performs shell operations on a managed EC2 instance. Management inbound ports must not be opened, and operators must be restricted through IAM. Connectivity to the SSM Agent and the required endpoints is already available. Which option should be used?

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: VPC Flow Logs collect communication records but do not provide shell connectivity.

choices.text: Use SSH through an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint
choices.explanation: This can eliminate the public path, but the guest still needs to accept SSH connections.

choices.text: Add a public bastion host
choices.explanation: This increases bastion-host and network management and maintains an SSH path.

choices.text: Use Systems Manager Session Manager
choices.explanation: It opens a session to the managed node without requiring an SSH port to remain continuously open.

learning.reason: A session can be opened to the managed node without keeping an SSH port continuously open.
learning.concept: The SSM Agent, an IAM role for the instance, and a communication path to Systems Manager are required.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Recovering from an Incorrect Update
prompt: At 14:00, multiple tables in a production RDS database were updated incorrectly. You need to compare the current data with the data at 13:59 within the backup retention period, without interrupting normal production processing. The only manual snapshot available is from the previous day. Which option should be chosen?

choices.text: Perform a manual Multi-AZ failover
choices.explanation: The update is replicated to the standby, so failover does not restore the database to an earlier point in time.

choices.text: Restart the current database
choices.explanation: Restarting the database does not undo incorrectly updated data.

choices.text: Restore a separate database from the previous day's manual snapshot
choices.explanation: Production can remain available, but the restored data will not be from the required time.

choices.text: Create a separate database using point-in-time restore
choices.explanation: A new database can be restored to the specified time within the backup retention period.

learning.reason: A new database can be restored to the specified time within the backup retention period.
learning.concept: PITR and high-availability failover are different capabilities. Check the backup retention period and the latest restorable time.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Detecting Missing Tags
prompt: For many existing EC2 instances and EC2 instances added in the future, you need to continuously evaluate configurations that lack required tags with fixed names and remediate them from a noncompliance list. Rejecting them only at creation time cannot cover the existing environment.

choices.text: An AWS Config rule
choices.explanation: It can evaluate resource configurations and identify resources that do not comply with the defined settings.

choices.text: Only use an SCP to reject new resource creation without the required tags
choices.explanation: This provides preventive control but does not continuously evaluate existing noncompliant resources.

choices.text: A CloudWatch CPU alarm
choices.explanation: CPU values do not determine whether tags are present.

choices.text: An AWS Budgets cost notification
choices.explanation: It alerts on spending and does not check required tags in resource configurations.

learning.reason: It can evaluate resource configurations and identify resources that do not comply with the defined settings.
learning.concept: AWS Config performs configuration detection and evaluation. If creation itself must be blocked, consider a separate preventive control for the relevant action.

title: Drift from an Existing Stack
prompt: EC2 and security groups are managed with CloudFormation. You suspect that changes were made manually and want to read-only check the differences between the actual values and the stack's expected values, limited to supported properties explicitly specified in the template.

choices.text: Loosen the CloudFormation stack policy
choices.explanation: This controls the scope of permitted updates; it does not detect drift.

choices.text: Only create a change set from the same template
choices.explanation: Creating a change set alone does not produce a list of differences from the actual configuration.

choices.text: Stack drift detection
choices.explanation: It can detect differences between expected properties and actual values.

choices.text: Only inspect the history of operation events in CloudTrail
choices.explanation: This can help identify who made changes, but it does not automatically compare current values with the definition.

learning.reason: It can detect differences between expected properties and actual values.
learning.concept: Drift detection applies to supported properties and does not correct differences merely because detection was run.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Notification and Automatic Recovery
prompt: OOM events occur intermittently on Linux EC2 instances. You need to turn each instance's guest OS memory utilization into metrics at one-minute intervals and investigate its correlation with CPU utilization. How should you do this without implementing custom monitoring code?

choices.text: Use the ALB target response time as a substitute for memory utilization
choices.explanation: It shows latency but does not measure utilization on the guest OS.

choices.text: Send guest OS memory metrics with CloudWatch Agent
choices.explanation: It can collect indicators from inside the guest OS as additional metrics.

choices.text: Only enable detailed monitoring for EC2
choices.explanation: This changes the granularity of standard metrics but does not add guest OS memory information.

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs
choices.explanation: They record network flows and do not collect memory utilization inside the OS.

learning.reason: It can collect indicators from inside the guest OS as additional metrics.
learning.concept: During analysis, also verify the collection interval, dimensions, and the agent's IAM permissions.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Monitoring Without Detaching Under High Load
prompt: EC2 instances behind an ALB temporarily respond slowly under high load because they are waiting for database connections. The current health check calls a heavy database query, causing all instances to be marked unhealthy simultaneously. You want to detect dead applications while notifying separately about shared database failures.

choices.text: Configure a lightweight process check for the ALB and monitor the database with a separate alarm
choices.explanation: This separates the detachment decision from operational notifications about the shared dependency.

choices.text: Only increase the health check timeout
choices.explanation: This may help with temporary latency but does not distinguish database failures from application failures.

choices.text: Change the ALB health check to an even heavier business operation
choices.explanation: This worsens the problem of all instances becoming unhealthy when the shared dependency fails.

choices.text: Treat all HTTP statuses as successful
choices.explanation: This would also treat responses from an unhealthy application as healthy.

learning.reason: This separates the detachment decision from operational notifications about the shared dependency.
learning.concept: Use different monitoring for the decision to remove an instance from load balancing and for notifications about dependency failures.

category: 監視、障害対応、運用自動化
title: Depleting Burst Performance
prompt: On an EC2 instance using gp2, I/O is temporarily fast when a large batch begins each day, but latency then increases sharply. CPU and memory have capacity available, and BurstBalance falls close to 0%. You want to provide stable IOPS without changing the capacity.

choices.text: Recreate a gp2 volume with the same capacity and replace it every day.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve insufficient baseline performance and increases operational overhead.

choices.text: Only reduce the frequency of EBS snapshots.
choices.explanation: This does not directly resolve depletion of the burst balance.

choices.text: Change the volume to gp3 and configure the IOPS and throughput required by the workload.
choices.explanation: Performance can be specified independently of the capacity and burst balance.

choices.text: Set the EC2 instance's CPU credits to Unlimited.
choices.explanation: The observed depletion concerns EBS I/O credits.

learning.reason: Performance can be specified independently of the capacity and burst balance.
learning.concept: When diagnosing I/O latency, check both the volume-side and instance-side performance limits.

title: Applying a New AMI to Existing Instances
prompt: An Auto Scaling group is running four EC2 instances. You have updated the launch template to use a new AMI and want to replace all existing instances while they continue receiving traffic.

choices.text: Change only the launch template.
choices.explanation: Existing EC2 instances are not replaced automatically.

choices.text: Restart all existing EC2 instances simultaneously.
choices.explanation: Restarting does not update the AMI.

choices.text: Specify the new launch template version, configure the minimum healthy percentage and warm-up, and run an Instance Refresh.
choices.explanation: This replaces the instances gradually with the new configuration while managing healthy capacity during the replacement.

choices.text: Only increase the group's maximum capacity.
choices.explanation: This does not perform a sequential replacement of the existing instances.

learning.reason: The instances can be replaced gradually with the new configuration while healthy capacity is managed during the replacement.
learning.concept: A launch template defines new launches; replacing existing instances requires a separate operation.

title: One-Way Reachability Failure Within a VPC
prompt: Communication between a client and a web server in different subnets of the same VPC times out. The server's security group already allows the traffic. You want to investigate whether the route and ACL to the destination ENI contain a configuration-based block.

choices.text: Check the EC2 CPUUtilization metric in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: CPU utilization does not indicate an allow or deny decision along the network path.

choices.text: Specify the source and destination, protocol, and port in VPC Reachability Analyzer.
choices.explanation: It analyzes the configuration and can identify routes or filters that prevent reachability.

choices.text: Only aggregate the number of ACCEPT entries in VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: Allowed records alone cannot identify the blocking point on the specified path from the configuration.

choices.text: Run curl from the server to localhost.
choices.explanation: This can verify the server process, but it does not test the route from another subnet.

learning.reason: The configuration can be analyzed to identify routes or filters that prevent reachability.
learning.concept: Reachability Analyzer analyzes configuration; whether the application responds must be verified separately with a communication test.
